title: No server left running
plain: The test makes a lab run crash and hang on purpose, then checks that no Minecraft server is still running and the port is free.
why: A forgotten server eats a gigabyte of memory and blocks the next run.
done_when: No server process and no held port after done, crash and stuck runs.

title: Only its own folder is deleted
plain: The reset step is asked to delete your real server folder and a random folder; it must refuse both and only clear its own scratch world.
why: Reset means deleting a world, so a wrong path could destroy real files.
done_when: Both bad paths are refused and the scratch world is cleared.

title: Memory gate before starting
plain: The lab is told memory is low, or three servers are already running, and must refuse to start another.
why: Servers and builds share 16 GB, and running out would freeze the computer.
done_when: Low memory and a fourth server are both refused.

title: Only finished chunks are read
plain: A hand-made chunk marked half-finished and a missing chunk are read; both must come back as unknown, not air.
why: Chunks next to a loaded one are only partly made, and reading them as air would fake a difference.
done_when: Half-made and missing chunks are reported unknown in every case.

title: Edge blocks read back exactly
plain: Blocks are placed at chunk borders, at negative coordinates, and at the lowest and highest heights, then read back after a save.
why: A reader that is wrong at the edges would invent differences exactly where chunks meet.
done_when: Every placed block reads back as the same block.

title: No Minecraft files in the repo
plain: The test scans the repo for region files, the server jar and world saves, and checks the ignore list blocks them.
why: Minecraft's files are not ours to publish, and the repo should stay small.
done_when: The scan finds zero Minecraft files and the ignore rules are present.

title: Only block types are compared
plain: Two worlds that differ only in timestamps, lighting or height maps are compared and must show zero differences; one changed block must show exactly one.
why: The question is about blocks, and other saved data changes every run.
done_when: Data-only changes give 0 and a single block change gives 1.

title: Same order twice comes first
plain: The report builder is given an order comparison with no repeat of the same order and must refuse to say order matters; if the repeat differs, it labels the result shaky.
why: If the same order disagrees with itself, no difference between orders can be believed.
done_when: No verdict without a same-order repeat, and shaky is flagged.

title: Waiting time is not order
plain: The same order is saved after a short wait and after a long wait on the real server, and the blocks are compared.
why: Water and sand keep moving after a chunk is made, which could look like an order effect.
done_when: The two saves give the same blocks, or the number that differs is reported.

title: Is the lever a player move
plain: Each step in a claimed lever is tagged as a player action or an admin command, and any admin command makes the lever lab-only.
why: Commands like forceload are not moves in a real run, so a lever that needs them is no use for a speedrun.
done_when: Admin-only levers are labelled lab-only and player ones are not.

title: More diamonds must replay
plain: A claimed gain is replayed twice in fresh worlds with the found order and compared with the default order from the same session.
why: A single lucky count would be mistaken for a lever.
done_when: Both replays match the claimed count and the default count is recorded.

title: Real routes obey the real rules
plain: Routes on the real terrain are replayed by a separate checker; mining iron with a wooden pickaxe or none must be rejected.
why: A route that breaks the game's rules is not a speedrun.
done_when: Every route passes the checker and the trap route is rejected.

title: Lava is not floor
plain: Every block name in the seed 7 area must have a known meaning, and lava, water and unknown names must never count as walkable floor.
why: A route across lava looks fast on paper and ends the run.
done_when: No unmapped block name and no unsafe block counted as floor.

title: The edge of the map is a wall
plain: A route that steps outside the area we read must be rejected.
why: We know nothing outside the area, so leaving it would invent shortcuts.
done_when: The route using unknown cells is rejected.

title: The rival route finder is fair
plain: Both route finders get the same terrain and the same budget, and on a small crop the rival must find the true best route.
why: Beating a weak rival proves nothing.
done_when: The rival matches the true best route on the crop with a large budget.

title: Website numbers come from files
plain: The test changes a saved result file and the page must change; a missing file must show not measured, never zero.
why: Zero differing blocks is a real answer, so a missing result must not look like it.
done_when: The page follows the file and a missing result reads not measured.

title: Route shown as not yet played
plain: The page must say the route was planned on the map and has not been played in the game.
why: Ticks on paper are not a finished speedrun, and the site should not suggest they are.
done_when: The unplayed label is on the page next to the route numbers.
